appendix_basis: Appendix J, standard monthly unit period; analogous to published Example A-1 structure
unit_period_analysis: Standard monthly unit period throughout. Payment 1 due at t=1, Payment 2 at t=2, …, Payment 36 at t=36. All unit periods = exactly 1 month. No fractional period at origination.

case_name: Irregular first period — 45-day gap before equal monthly payments
appendix_basis: Appendix J Section J-3 / J-4 (fractional first period); irregular-period transaction rule
unit_period_analysis: Irregular first period: 45 days ÷ 30 days = 1.5 standard months (fractional unit period at origination). First payment is at t=1.5. Subsequent payments are at t=2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 5.5. Each full month thereafter counts as 1 unit period.

computation.description: Express payment times in unit periods

weakest_point: The 30-day-per-month convention is the standard Appendix J approach for irregular periods, but some implementations use actual calendar days (365/12) which yields a slightly different fractional period. The interpolation method (linear between discrete rates) is the approach Appendix J's iterative method approximates; exact result could differ by 0.01–0.03 pp in the APR.

appendix_basis: Appendix J Section J-2 (single advance, single payment; direct APR formula)
unit_period_analysis: Single-payment transaction: APR = Finance Charge ÷ Amount Financed × (365 ÷ Days to maturity). No iteration required; closed-form solution.
weakest_point: The single-payment formula is Appendix J's most mechanically straightforward rule. Minor ambiguity: whether the APR is rounded to the nearest 1/8% or to the nearest 1/4% under the tolerance rules — but the actuarial result of 12.17% is exact before any disclosure rounding.

case_name: Irregular payment schedule — declining payments over 10 months
appendix_basis: Appendix J Section J-3 (multiple advances/payments, irregular schedule); acts as Example J-5 analog
unit_period_analysis: All payments align with monthly unit periods from origination (t=1,2,…,10). No fractional first period. Each payment discounted by (1+r)^(-k) where k is the month number.
weakest_point: This is a constructed example illustrating the irregular-multiple-payment structure under Appendix J; it is not a verified published example number from the official document. The specific payment amounts and schedule are chosen for clean arithmetic; a published example would have different numbers. The interpolation between r=0.009 and r=0.010 is linear approximation — the true iterative solution would be very close (within 0.001 pp).
